relationships.detail: husband / wife
relationships.source: UBF's own served Fridaynight Warfare results text (18 August 2000): a backstage line addressed to Cameron Spayze -- "Those aren't for her! Those are for Mrs. Pearson!" -- naming the same surname (Pearson) shared by both Jett Pearson and Donna Pearson, the two people the scene and the later backstage brawl separately name.

relationships.detail: Firebrand kidnapped El Triton's son to force a challenge for the Baja Blast Championship Sponsored by Taco Bell; El Triton beat him for the title at Run for the Border, refusing Firebrand's demanded pledge of service in the process.
relationships.source: promotions/adw/archive/season-recap.html; promotions/adw/archive/run-for-the-border.html

relationships.detail: The Void's own interference cost El Professor the vacant title in a three-way; the two fought to a Steel Cage draw for the #1 contendership, then rematched at Run for the Border, El Professor winning by being first out of the collapsing cage.
relationships.source: promotions/adw/archive/season-recap.html; promotions/adw/archive/run-for-the-border.html

relationships.detail: BEW President Michael Merrix directly names Kevin Merrix his own brother on-air ("my successful brother Kevin Merrix just signed a very lucrative contract" with the GWF), and Big Hughy independently taunts Michael with the same claim ("your worthless brother") earlier the same broadcast.
relationships.source: promotions/bew/archive/night-of-armageddon.html

relationships.detail: Billed "his once bad boy brother" — the fed's own commentary frames the two as former bitter enemies, "now closest of allies," reunited for the show's own closing save on Kevin Merrix.
relationships.source: promotions/bew/archive/night-of-armageddon.html

relationships.detail: Michael Duncan's aide, addressed only by rank — present in all four of Duncan's End of an Era III roleplays, bringing the wine, driving the car, dealing the cards and reading the map.
relationships.source: promotions/pwe-inc/archive/1-in-cont-s-match-2005-12-10.html — the fed's own number one contender's roleplay thread of 10 December 2005

relationships.detail: David D's mouthpiece — writes and speaks all four of David D's roleplays for End of an Era III himself, the wrestler never once answering in his own voice.

relationships.detail: Balthamel's manager and mouthpiece — called the FoB Heavyweight Championship worthless, was hit over the head with his own microphone, and was finally knocked off the apron by his own client.

relationships.detail: Walked to the ring with Fight Against Prejudice on 13 October 2005 and nodded to “his two clients” when the beating was finished; Dutt is the other.

relationships.detail: SCW World Tag Team Champions together; the Monsta Boyz took the titles from them.
relationships.source: EUWC's own roster bio card for Dan Ryan (promotions/euwc/archive/bio-dan-ryan.html): "Ryan competed in SCW and won the World Tag Team Titles along with partner 'Mr. Main Event' Rob Sampson"; the Monsta Boyz's own roster card in GWA (promotions/gwa-gateway-2004/archive/the-monsta-boyz-2004-09-23.html), the other side of the same reign: "a brief stint in SCW where they defeated Rob Sampson and Dan Ryan for the Superior Tag Titles, only to retire them when the promotion closed a month or so later"; and Dan Ryan's own bio as GWA (26 September 2004), UCW (13 July 2006), TEAM and PRIME serve it, each listing "SCW World Tag Team Champion (w/Rob Sampson)" or "SCW: World Tag Team Titles (w/Rob Sampson)".
relationships.note: The Rob Sampson of these cards is rob-sampson-cswa: EUWC's card bills him "Mr. Main Event" Rob Sampson, this record's own billing, and the two men's careers run through the same feds (CSWA, GXW, EUWC, Empire Pro). The copies of Ryan's bio from 2006 on (UCW's of 13 July 2006, EUWC's, TEAM's, PRIME's) name his second finisher, the Headliner, a Burning Hammer "in homage to late friend" Rob Sampson (UCW's: "late friend 'Main Event' Rob Sampson"). SCW itself is not a held wing; which SCW it was is not established (the Monsta Boyz's card calls its belts the Superior Tag Titles).
